text: Skip to main content Progeni Bench . Nothing is uploaded. MP3 WAV FLAC AAC/M4A FFmpeg engine 100.00 MB / file 1. Add a file Drop an audio file here or click to browse. Files stay on this device. 2. Settings OUTPUT FORMAT MP3 (.mp3) WAV (.wav) M4A / AAC (.m4a) OGG Vorbis (.ogg) Opus (.opus) FLAC (.flac) AIFF (.aiff) MP3, M4A, OGG and Opus are lossy. WAV, FLAC and AIFF are lossless and much larger. BITRATE (KBPS) 96 - small files 128 - standard 160 192 - good 256 - high 320 - maximum MP3 Applies to lossy formats only. Ignored for WAV, FLAC and AIFF. CHANNELS Keep original Mono (1 channel) Stereo (2 channels) Mono halves the data for spoken audio. Converting stereo to mono mixes the channels. SAMPLE RATE Keep original 22,050 Hz 44,100 Hz (CD) 48,000 Hz (video) Lowering the sample rate reduces size but discards high frequencies. Process Reset Ready. Processing happens locally in this tab. 3. Results Play Stop 0:00.00 No results yet Bench creates real output only. What it does Decodes your file and re-encodes it in the format you choose using the FFmpeg.wasm engine that runs on your device. Lossy formats expose a bitrate control; lossless formats keep every sample. The result is validated, played back for comparison and offered as a download with its true byte size. How to use Add an MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR or WMA file. Bench decodes it and shows duration, sample rate and channels. Pick the output format. Choose a bitrate for lossy formats or a lower sample rate to save space. Run the converter. The engine is downloaded the first time and cached afterwards. Preview the result and download it. If the requested format is unavailable, Bench says so instead of faking the output. Common use cases Turn a WAV recording into a small MP3. Convert an M4A voice memo to WAV for editing. Produce a FLAC master from a lossless source. Limits & considerations MP3 output uses libmp3lame and AAC uses FFmpeg's encoder; both are lossy and re-encoding lossy audio again can add artefacts. Very long files are bounded by the 30-minute / 100 MB limits. The first conversion downloads the ~31 MB engine. Privacy & security Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device. Frequently asked questions Which formats can I convert between? MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG Vorbis, Opus and AIFF in any direction the encoder supports, plus decoding of AMR, WMA, Speex and more. Why is the first conversion slow? The FFmpeg.wasm engine (~31 MB) is downloaded once and cached by your browser. Later conversions start instantly. Does converting lose quality? Converting to WAV, FLAC or AIFF is lossless. Converting to MP3, AAC, OGG or Opus is lossy; converting lossy to lossy can add artefacts, so start from the best source you have. text: Skip to main content Progeni Bench . Every tool below has a real client-side handler and a tested download path. Tools that are not ready are labelled honestly instead of pretending to work. 43 implemented tools 5 experimental No account No uploads Start with the Audio Trimmer Browse all Bench tools Convert & Compress Change format, bitrate and size between MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC, OGG, Opus, M4A and AIFF. Audio Converter Convert between MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus and AIFF with a real encoder and an exact output size. Implemented and tested Audio Compressor Reduce an audio file's size by lowering bitrate, downmixing to mono and trimming the sample rate. Implemented and tested Cut, Join & Edit Trim, split, merge, fade, reverse, change speed and loudness. Audio Trimmer Cut a section out of an audio file with an interactive waveform and export the exact range. Implemented and tested Audio Splitter Split one file into several parts by time or into equal-length chunks, exported together. Implemented and tested Fade In / Out Add a fade-in, a fade-out or both to smooth the start and end of a track. Implemented and tested Crossfade Editor Blend two tracks together with a real crossfade at a duration you choose. Implemented and tested Stereo & Channel Tools Swap or merge channels, isolate left or right, downmix to mono or make a dual-mono track. Implemented and tested Clean & Enhance Reduce noise and hum, normalise loudness, EQ, limit and detect clipping. Silence Remover Detect silent gaps and remove them, or keep the gaps but trim the leading and trailing silence. Implemented and tested Volume & Normalize Change the loudness by a fixed amount or normalise to a target peak, with clipping protection. Implemented and tested Noise Reducer Reduce steady background noise (hiss, hum, air conditioning) with a real FFT denoiser. Experimental Voice Enhancer Brighten and control speech with a high-pass, EQ and gentle compression chain. Experimental Bass, Treble & EQ Boost or cut bass, treble and a selectable mid band with real peaking filters. Implemented and tested Loudness Normalizer (LUFS) Normalise to a broadcast loudness target in LUFS with true-peak limiting. Implemented and tested Record & Microphone Record from your microphone locally, meter input and test channels. Voice Recorder Record from your microphone in the browser, preview it and download a WAV or WebM/Opus file. Implemented and tested BPM & Key Detector Estimate the tempo (BPM) of a track and suggest a likely musical key from its spectrum. Experimental Spectrogram / Spectrum Analyzer Render a spectrogram or real-time spectrum of a file to see its frequencies over time. Implemented and tested Metadata & Diagnostics Inspect and edit tags, measure loudness, peaks, bitrate and integrity. Clipping Detector Scan a file for clipped samples and report where and how often it distorts. Implemented and tested Silence Detector Map every silent gap in a file with start time, end time and duration. Implemented and tested Audio Metadata Viewer Inspect ID3/tags, duration, bitrate, sample rate, channels and codec of an audio file. Implemented and tested ID3 Tag Editor View and rewrite common ID3/tag fields (title, artist, album, genre) and export a new copy. Experimental Loudness & Peak Analyzer Measure integrated LUFS, true peak, RMS and dynamic range for broadcast or streaming checks. Implemented and tested Audio Integrity Check Verify a file decodes cleanly and report header, signature and structure problems. Implemented and tested Duplicate Audio Finder Compare several audio files and find exact duplicates using a content hash. Implemented and tested Developer Utilities Base64, data URIs, waveform images, player snippets and batch export. Audio to Base64 Encode an audio file as a Base64 string or a data URI for embedding in code. Implemented and tested Base64 to Audio Decode a Base64 string or data URI back into a playable, downloadable audio file. Implemented and tested Audio Batch Rename Rename and export several audio files at once with a prefix, sequence numbers and a chosen format. Implemented and tested Audio to ZIP Bundle several audio files into a single ZIP archive for one-click download. Implemented and tested Waveform Image Generate a clean waveform image (PNG) from any audio file for video, print or the web. Implemented and tested Audio MIME & Signature Checker See the real file type from its magic bytes and compare it with the extension and reported MIME type. Implemented and tested HTML Audio Player Generator Generate a safe, accessible HTML <audio> player snippet for your file. Implemented and tested Podcast RSS Enclosure Validator Check a podcast RSS feed's <enclosure> tags for missing or invalid audio URLs and types. Implemented and tested Status and limits Implemented tools are covered by automated tests and produce real files. Experimental tools run real signal processing but have documented quality caveats; their results should be checked before important use. Limits: 100 MB per file, 30 minutes per file, 20 files per batch. Conversion and complex filters use a 31 MB FFmpeg engine downloaded once and cached. How processing works Simple editing, analysis, recording and WAV export use the Web Audio API directly in the tab. Format conversion and complex filters (loudness normalisation, denoise, speed, EQ) use a WebAssembly build of FFmpeg that runs on your device. Either way, the audio bytes never leave your machine and Bench keeps no copy. Licences and source The FFmpeg engine shipped here is the official @ffmpeg/core build, licensed under the GNU General Public License v2.0 or later. It is served unmodified from this site at /vendor/ffmpeg/ and is never loaded from a third-party CDN. The JavaScript wrapper (@ffmpeg/ffmpeg) is MIT licensed. Full attributions, exact version numbers and a written offer to supply the corresponding source code are published in /vendor/ffmpeg/NOTICE.txt. That notice names the upstream FFmpeg project and the ffmpeg.wasm packaging project, including their source repositories. Not available yet These entries exist so the catalogue stays honest. No page is generated for them and no upload control is offered. Audio Transcription Deferred Requires a speech-recognition model (e.g. Whisper). Running it in-browser needs a large model download and the site's CSP blocks external APIs (connect-src 'self'). Ship a verified adapter before publishing a page. Text to Speech Unavailable The browser SpeechSynthesis API can speak text but cannot reliably capture the output to a file, so a real downloadable MP3/WAV is not possible without a TTS engine or provider. Not offered rather than faked. Vocal Remover / Stem Separation Deferred Requires a real source-separation model (e.g. Demucs/Spleeter). A centre-channel cancellation is not genuine separation, so this is deferred until a licensed model can be shipped. AI Noise Reduction Deferred Requires a licensed neural model. The shipped afftdn denoiser is real spectral processing, not AI, and is offered honestly as the Noise Reducer instead. Audio Restoration Deferred Needs a restoration model. Deterministic filters (declick, declip) exist in the engine and could ship as an experimental tool; full restoration is deferred. Speaker Diarization Unavailable Depends on a speaker-recognition model and, typically, a transcript. No local model is shipped, so labels cannot be produced from real results. Speech Translation Deferred Depends on transcription plus a translation service. External APIs are blocked by the site's CSP, so this is deferred with transcription. System / Tab Audio Capture Deferred getDisplayMedia with audio capture is not supported consistently across browsers and platforms. Deferred rather than shipped with silent failures. Blends them into a 0-100 composite score with adjustable weights and shows the sharpness/exposure/contrast breakdown per photo, a full ranked list with load-more, and a side-by-side compare of the top shots.
